title: SAP Automotive JIT / JIS Domain Model

meta.summary: Architecture-level model of classic SAP Automotive JIT and Next Generation JIT, with business objects, lifecycle controls, integration boundaries, and design rules.

attribution.preferred_citation: Dzmitryi Kharlanau, SAP Automotive JIT / JIS Domain Model, Assessment Lab.

provenance.method: Structured from SAP Help documentation and practitioner-oriented architecture synthesis.

purpose.human: Prepare for SAP Lead assessment and solution-design discussions without memorizing isolated transactions.
purpose.agent: Give an AI agent a stable ontology for requirements analysis, specification review, integration design, diagnostics, and architecture recommendations.
purpose.core_question: What demand signal is received, what object represents it, what controls its lifecycle, what must happen next, and which system owns each decision?

terminology.meaning: Just-In-Time. Material is requested for a short delivery horizon and should arrive close to the point of use.
Just-In-Sequence. A sequenced JIT call where the supplier must deliver in the production sequence requested by the customer.
Classic SAP term for sequenced JIT call. It normally carries vehicle or order reference and sequence information.
Classic SAP term for summarized JIT call. Demand is mainly date/quantity based and is not sequence-specific.
Delivery Order Number. In summarized JIT processing, the reference number can control downstream processing such as delivery.
Not treated here as a canonical SAP Automotive JIT term. If a project uses JIC, the specification must define the local meaning before an agent maps it to SAP objects.
terminology.agent_rule: Never silently replace JIC with JIS. Ask or infer only from an explicit project glossary.

classic_jit.positioning: Established SAP Automotive JIT model used in SAP ERP and available in SAP S/4HANA on-premise documentation. The main mental model is Inbound JIT + Call Control + optional Outbound JIT.

inbound.business_role: Supplier receives JIT calls from an OEM or customer and supplies them.

call_types.use_when: The customer needs configured assemblies or materials for a particular vehicle/order in a defined sequence.
The customer sends date/quantity requirements without finished-product reference and without sequence delivery.

key_dependencies: destinations such as unloading point or assembly location
sales scheduling agreement context where used

call_control.definition: A configurable state/action engine for processing component groups.
call_control.logic: An action is allowed or triggered for a processing status. After the action succeeds, the component group receives the next processing status.
call_control.design_rule: Model business progression first, then map statuses and actions. Do not start from transaction codes.
call_control.why_it_matters: It separates business state from technical message receipt and allows different component groups to follow different control logic.
lead_questions: Which status comes from the customer and which status is internal?
Which transitions are automatic, manual, or exceptional?
Is an action idempotent if the same EDI message is received twice?
What is the recovery action after partial success?
Which status makes a call delivery-relevant?

outbound.business_role: A system supplier forwards or creates JIT demand for its own suppliers.

patterns.description: Relevant information from the inbound sequenced call is transformed into an outbound sequenced call for Tier-2 or sub-suppliers.
Summarized supplier demand can be created from supply-to-production logic or manually, depending on the process.

outbound.classic_integration: EDI using IDoc; additional MM, PP, LE and master-data functions participate depending on the scenario.

next_generation_jit.positioning: Newer S/4HANA JIT model with Supply to Customer (S2C) and Supply to Production (S2P) capabilities, Fiori applications, modern integration, and tighter E2E integration with logistics execution.

s2c.commercial_anchor: Sales scheduling agreement or other outline agreement provides the long-term commercial/planning relationship.
2025_fps01_highlights: End-to-end JIS integration with EWM and TM
Tier-2 supplier integration through JIS call forwarding

s2p.perspective: Manufacturer replenishing production from a warehouse or external supplier.
s2p.trigger: Demand from production, for example planned/production orders or consumption-driven replenishment.
s2p.object_context: A JIT call contains quantity, date/time, destination production supply area, destination storage location, material, partner and scheduling-agreement information.
s2p.jis_context: A sequenced call can be connected to a vehicle planned order and production sequence.

integration.inbound_service_example: SOAP service JITCallRequest_In for electronic receipt of customer JIT calls; SAP documents mapping through SAP Cloud Integration for S/4HANA Cloud.
integration.warehouse_and_transport: Next Generation JIT can integrate with LE-SHP, Handling Unit Management, EWM and TM for end-to-end JIS execution.
integration.architecture_rule: Select the JIT generation that matches the target S/4HANA release and scope. Do not copy classic IDoc-era design decisions into Next Generation JIT without checking supported APIs and process objects.

business_objects.role: Primary operational control unit in classic JIT; groups materials/assembly information and carries processing control.
Control master data used to connect material replenishment and source/destination logic; especially important for outbound and S2P scenarios.
Long-term commercial/planning anchor. Forecast and JIT/JIS signals refine the near-term execution requirement.
Next Generation JIS master/control object used to manage delivery sequence behavior and related checks.
Represents planned packing of component groups for sequenced customer JIT calls; can support sequence-controlled handling-unit execution.

decision_model.question: Is delivery order-specific and sequence-specific?
decision_model.yes: Use sequenced JIT / JIS mental model.

decision_model.question: Are we supplier-to-OEM, manufacturer-to-production, or Tier-1-to-Tier-2?
decision_model.why: The same word JIT can mean different ownership, contracts, and message directions.

decision_model.question: Is the target solution classic JIT or Next Generation JIT?
decision_model.why: Objects, applications, integration technology and extensibility differ.

decision_model.question: What is the source of truth for sequence and requested time?
decision_model.why: A technically valid message is useless if sequence authority is unclear.

decision_model.question: What happens if a sequence changes after production or packing has started?
decision_model.why: Resequencing is a business exception with physical consequences, not just a database update.

design_principles: Separate forecast/planning signals from execution calls.
Treat external status as input, not as the complete internal process state.
Keep message mapping separate from business lifecycle logic.
Make duplicate, change, cancel and resequence behavior explicit in the interface contract.
Model the physical flow together with the SAP document flow: sequence, packing, handling unit, loading, transport and line-side consumption are linked.
Prefer released APIs, BAdIs and key-user/developer extensibility over modifications; verify the exact target release before naming an extension point in a design.
Design monitoring and recovery before go-live. In JIT, a six-minute interface delay can be more important than a six-hour batch failure elsewhere.

classic_reference_transactions.note: Useful for orientation in classic JIT only. They are not an architecture.
